resources.string: Light or dark, for the settings app and the Default theme
Follows the light and dark setting of your device
Always light, whatever your device is set to
Always dark, whatever your device is set to
Dark, with a true black background. This saves battery on an OLED screen
The Default theme takes its colors from your wallpaper

The keyboard takes the colors of the app that you type in. It finds them in the app icon and in the colors that the app sets for its own screens. Then it makes a full palette from one of them, as Android does from your wallpaper. Your theme does not change. In a different app, or with this setting off, the keyboard shows the theme again. In the Appearance tool on the keyboard, you can select a different color of the app, or no color, for each app.
Use the colors of the app that you type in
The Default theme, and themes with Follow wallpaper colors on. Other themes keep their colors.
Every theme takes the app colors, also themes with fixed colors. Light and dark parts of the theme stay light and dark.
The colors that the app sets for its screens first, then the app icon
Only the app icon. Use this if the colors of an app look wrong.
Only the colors that the app sets for its screens, for example its toolbar. Some apps set none.
How one app color becomes a full palette
Calm colors. Android uses this style by default.
Colors moved away from the app color, for a playful look
Stays nearest to the exact app color
Almost gray, with a small quantity of color
Colored accents moved away from the app color

resources.string: The keyboard changes between a light theme and a dark theme on its own. While this is on, the theme tool on the keyboard shows only a preview. The schedule selects the active theme.
Use a light theme in the day and a dark theme at night
Select the themes you want. The keyboard shows one of them at a time.
How often a random half selects a new theme
Select a new theme from your sets
Changes with the light and dark setting of your device
Changes at two times that you set
Changes at sunrise and sunset where you are. This needs a saved location
The keyboard follows the light and dark setting of your device. This includes any schedule that Android runs for it.
The light theme shows between sunrise and sunset at %1$s. Your device calculates the times without a network connection.
No location is saved yet. Set one in the settings of the weather tool. Until then the keyboard uses the light and dark setting of your device.
Inherit: use the theme that is set
Select every look in this family
Auto theme is on, so the gallery only shows what it would look like.
High contrast keys is on, so the keyboard uses its own key, background and hint colors instead of the colors of this theme.
These parts of the keyboard use a theme of their own instead of this one: %1$s.
How a theme with more than one look shows
Follows the answer you gave in the setup questions
A theme with more than one look shows as one card. Press a dot on the card to use that look
Every look of every theme shows as its own card

The colors, key shape and background come from the picture. The app cannot copy a font or the icons on the keys. To rebuild a photo background better, pick up to three screenshots of the same keyboard, such as letters and symbols.
Also copy the sizes: number row, key height, gaps and the space under the keys
This picture is small, so thin lines and small labels may be missed. A full screenshot works better.
This copy does not match the picture closely. Check it before you use it.
The app did not find a keyboard in that picture. Use a screenshot that shows all the letter keys.
The app saved the theme with your themes.
This uses the same library as the document scanner. Download it to continue.
That file is not a WM Keyboard theme.
This deletes the look %1$s from this theme. The other looks stay.
Copy only %1$s, or the whole group of looks?
Material You, follows light and dark
Show the keyboard at full size
This theme does not exist any more.
The app makes all the colors from one seed color. You can change each color below.
The seed color makes a dark palette or a light palette
The colors change to match your wallpaper. Each color keeps its lightness, so the text stays easy to read.

The colors below are the colors that the theme stores. With this on, the keyboard shows them in your wallpaper colors. Turn it off to get the stored colors back. A color that you change here keeps its new value only if the theme came from a FlorisBoard file that names wallpaper colors; in all other themes, the new color also changes to match the wallpaper.
The keyboard paints this instead of the solid background color

The color behind the bars above and below the keys. This is the suggestion strip, the toolbar row, the emoji row, the symbol row, the dictionary bar, the fancy text bar and the selection macros. On Auto the bars show the board color, or the board image or gradient. The words on the strip keep their color from the board. If you make this color very different from the board, also set Suggestion text in the Panels and suggestions group.
The color of the band below the keys, where the system navigation bar is. On Auto the band shows the board color, or the board image or gradient. Phones with hardware buttons have no band.
None. Press to select a photo
The board color became transparent when you selected this image. The image shows at full strength. Increase the opacity of the background color to tint the image or to make it dark.
Optional: the keyboard shows this image in landscape, or the image above if this one is empty
The keyboard paints this sheen over the letter keys
Make every key match the letter keys
Shift, ?123, the emoji and tool keys and Enter take the letter keys\' colours. You can change each one after.
This colors the shift key when it is on, the active tools, and the buttons in the panels.
Uses the placement from the keyboard settings
The bubble grows out of the key that you press
The bubble floats above the key, apart from it
Chips are the small buttons in the tool panels: style pickers, converters, plugin buttons. Their background color is the card color above.
The fill behind the tools: their own row, and the suggestion strip while it shows the tools. On Auto it matches the suggestion strip.
The suggestions beside the main one on the strip. On Auto they use the suggestion text colour.
How big the other suggestions are, as a share of the main one.
The quieter text beside the main text: the second word of a suggestion, and the kind and time of a clipboard entry.
The thin lines between the parts of a panel, and between suggestions.
The colour of the shadow under each key. Leave it unset for the usual black, or pick a colour and lower its alpha for a soft glow. Android 8 and older draw every shadow black.
How far the keys are lifted off the board. Some key shapes cannot draw a shadow and stay flat, and so does a key whose colour you can see through.
The colour behind the letter your finger is on when you hold a key, and behind the selected row of the language list.
The strip beside the keyboard in one-handed mode. On Auto it stays clear, so the board shows through it.
Off: the theme follows the sliders in Appearance
A theme can set its own sizes and spacing, so one import changes the whole look. Screen-specific sizes from Layout settings still win over the theme.
Off: the theme follows the sliders in Appearance and Layout

Frosted glass: keys, bars and popups show what is behind them, blurred, with a rim of light and a little grain. Blurring the app behind the keyboard needs Android 12 or later and follows the phone\'s own blur setting. Over a background image the glass blurs the image instead, on every phone.
See-through surfaces over a blurred backdrop, with a rim and grain
A preset sets the glass sliders and makes the key, chip, tool and popup colors see-through where they are not already. Every slider still moves afterwards.
A pane of milky glass: what is behind it, blurred, under the surface\'s color

A thick lens: what is behind it bends at the edge, its colors split a little there, and the edge catches the light. Android 13 and later, over an image or the wallpaper; older phones and the blurred app draw it frosted
How far the backdrop is pulled inward near the edge of each pane, the way a thick lens magnifies what it covers. The middle always shows straight through.
How far red and blue part where the pane bends the backdrop, like light through the edge of a prism.
The app behind the keyboard shows through the board, blurred. Android 12 and later. Off while the phone\'s blur or the keyboard\'s power saving is off, and in the floating keyboard

This phone isn\'t blurring windows right now: its blur is off, or it has none. The glass shows your wallpaper instead of the app, so the background won\'t change from app to app. Look for a window blur switch in the phone\'s settings, or turn off battery saver.
How far the system blurs the app behind the board, and the keys behind a popup or menu.

The least opaque the board is drawn when the phone cannot blur behind it: an older Android, battery saver, the floating keyboard. The keys were made over a blur, and this keeps them readable without one.
The background image if the theme has one, otherwise your wallpaper whenever the app behind is not being blurred
The theme\'s background image, or nothing
Your wallpaper, always, even where the app could be blurred instead
Only each surface\'s own see-through color, its rim and its grain
Allow storage access so the glass can show the wallpaper itself. Without it, the glass paints soft shapes in the wallpaper\'s colors
Android 13 and later keep the wallpaper\'s picture private from apps, so the glass paints soft shapes in the wallpaper\'s own colors instead.
Backdrop blur, saturation and brightness need something behind the glass to blur. With nothing there, the glass is each surface\'s own see-through color, its rim and its grain.
The board takes your wallpaper\'s accent colour, as FrostKeys does. Off keeps a darker, quieter tint in the wallpaper\'s hue
The background image is frosted between the keys as well, with the backdrop sliders below. Off keeps it as sharp as its own blur setting leaves it
How much the background image is blurred where it shows through a glass surface. The board itself stays as sharp as its own blur setting leaves it.
A hairline of light along the top-left edge of each surface and of shadow along the bottom-right.
An animation runs only while the keyboard is on the screen.
Turns the colors of the gradient, or the solid board color
Plays a GIF or animated WebP background. Turns off blur. Does not play with reduce motion or power saving.
The pin on each card decides if the theme shows in the keyboard\'s Themes tool. Your own themes always show there.
Remove %1$s from the keyboard\'s theme list
Show %1$s in the keyboard\'s theme list
An image drawn on the keys, clipped to the key shape, over the key color. One image for the letter keys is enough. The other keys reuse it unless you give them their own.
How the image fits a key
Fills the key and cuts off what does not fit
Fills the key and changes the shape of the image
Repeats the image at its own size
Give one key a style of its own: its colors, a texture, the burst it throws, and how its label is drawn. A letter keeps its style on every layout that has it.
Type a letter, or choose one of the special keys.
No image, tap to choose one
Press a key, a tool or the suggestion strip on the preview to style it
Undo the last change to this theme
Press a key, a tool or the strip
The bar above the keys has a section of its own for each of its two faces, and so do the popups. Pressing a tool or a suggestion on the preview opens the same sections, under the preview.
The bubble over a pressed key and the press and hold alternates
Tap a part to style it
Strip fill, word colors and size
Images laid over the keys, only for decoration. Typing goes through them. Transparent PNG images work best.
A small burst of particles under every key press. It does not play with reduce motion or power saving.
Your own particle images, up to six. Each press throws a random mix of them. Transparent PNG images work best.
Every emoji or image keeps its own colours
One flat colour, the same as the key labels
One flat colour, the accent of this theme
One flat colour, the same as the glide trail
One flat colour that you pick below
A different colour for every particle
Natural keeps each emoji or image in its own colours. Every other choice paints the particles one flat colour, so a glyph becomes a silhouette.
How fast the particles fall. Zero leaves them drifting, and below zero they float upward.

The theme can bring its own key font and key sound. If the device does not have them, the keyboard uses your global choices. Fonts and sounds install as add-ons, so you can also use them with other themes.
Add a font for a script
The key font above is used for Latin, Cyrillic and Greek. Other scripts keep their own font unless the theme gives them one.
Every script already has a font in this theme.
The colors run in a straight line, at the angle below
The colors run out from the center in rings
The colors turn around the center like a clock hand
Pinch to zoom, drag to move the image
Color wheel. Drag to set the hue and the saturation.
Sizes for backgrounds, key images and stickers, with templates to draw on
These sizes come from the keyboard itself, measured for the screen you select. Draw at the template size. The keyboard makes larger images smaller.
Your layout and your key sizes on this screen
A common 1080 pixel wide phone with the default sizes. Use this for a theme you share.
The same phone turned on its side, for the landscape background
A 1600 pixel wide tablet or an open foldable, with the default sizes
The board template: the outline of each key over the background area

Save images as PNG to keep transparent areas. The template files are transparent, with white lines: put them on the top layer of your drawing and hide them before you export. Key images fill the key and are cut to its shape, so keep the important parts in the middle. The keyboard crops the background from the center, so an image with the same shape as the board shows fully.
%1$d × %2$d px on screen. Draw at %3$d × %4$d px.
The whole keyboard, with the toolbar at the top. The band at the bottom is under the navigation bar, and shows only on Android 15 and later.
Shift, delete and the other function keys have a different width. The template is the most common key.
The keyboard keeps up to 1024 × 320 pixels of a space bar image.
The bubble that shows the key you press. Its height follows the popup height of the theme.
Transparent PNG, up to 512 pixels on the long side. The size shown is the default sticker width, and you can change it.
Transparent PNG, square. The keyboard keeps up to 192 pixels of each image.
